# apple_beta_group_build (Resource)

Gives one TestFlight group one build — the distribution half of `fastlane pilot distribute`, and what a group without `has_access_to_all_builds` needs before its testers can install anything.

The build is named the way a pipeline already names it, by `build_number` and `pre_release_version` rather than by Apple's opaque build ID, exactly as `apple_beta_build_localization` does. The group's app is read from the group, so no `app_id` is needed.

Like `apple_beta_tester`, this is a **linkage, not a record**: destroying it takes the build away from this group's testers and leaves the build, and every other group it was given to, alone.

Apple refuses a build that has not finished processing; wait for `VALID` first, with `apple build wait`. A group with `has_access_to_all_builds` already receives every build and is refused here at apply.

~> For an **external** group, assigning a build is not the same as testers seeing it: Apple's beta review must approve the build first, and submitting it is not modelled — it is an event rather than state. Submit from App Store Connect.

~> Terraform does not upload builds. The binary must already be in App Store Connect, put there by `apple build upload`, Xcode or Transporter.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

variable "build_number" {
  description = "CFBundleVersion of the build already uploaded to App Store Connect (CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)."
  type        = string
  default     = "42"
}

variable "marketing_version" {
  description = "CFBundleShortVersionString of the build's train (MARKETING_VERSION)."
  type        = string
  default     = "1.4.0"
}

# A group that chooses its builds rather than receiving every one.
resource "apple_beta_group" "release_candidates" {
  app_id                   = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  name                     = "Release candidates"
  is_internal_group        = true
  has_access_to_all_builds = false
}

# Gives the group the build a pipeline just uploaded and waited for:
#
#   apple build upload build/App.ipa
#   apple build wait "$version" "$build"
#   TF_VAR_build_number="$build" TF_VAR_marketing_version="$version" terraform apply
#
# Changing build_number replaces the assignment: the previous build comes off
# the group and the new one goes on. Apple refuses a build that is still
# processing.
resource "apple_beta_group_build" "release_candidate" {
  group_id            = apple_beta_group.release_candidates.id
  build_number        = var.build_number
  pre_release_version = var.marketing_version
}

# An external group's testers see an assigned build only after Apple's beta
# review approves it, and submitting it for review stays in App Store Connect.
resource "apple_beta_group" "early_access" {
  app_id = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  name   = "Early access"
}

resource "apple_beta_group_build" "early_access" {
  group_id            = apple_beta_group.early_access.id
  build_number        = var.build_number
  pre_release_version = var.marketing_version
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `build_number` (String) The build number of the uploaded build — `CFBundleVersion`, which a pipeline knows as `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`. Dot-separated numbers, such as `42` or `1.2.3`. Naming a different build replaces the assignment: the old build comes off the group and the new one goes on.
- `group_id` (String) The Apple ID of the `apple_beta_group` to give the build to. Giving it to a different group is a different assignment and replaces the resource.
- `pre_release_version` (String) The marketing version of the build train — `CFBundleShortVersionString`, which a pipeline knows as `MARKETING_VERSION`.

### Optional

- `platform` (String) Which platform's build to take: `IOS`, `MAC_OS`, `TV_OS` or `VISION_OS`. Only needed when the same train and build number exist on more than one platform; left unset, the lookup is not narrowed.

### Read-Only

- `build_id` (String) The Apple ID of the build, resolved from `build_number` and `pre_release_version`.
- `id` (String) `<group_id>/<build_id>`. Apple has no identifier for an assignment, so this is composed from the two it links.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# An assignment is imported as "<group_id>/<pre_release_version>/<build_number>",
# naming the build the way the configuration does.
terraform import apple_beta_group_build.release_candidate "4f1a9c30-7b52-4e18-9d66-2c8a3f5e1b04/1.4.0/42"

# Add the platform second when the same train and build number exist on more
# than one platform.
terraform import apple_beta_group_build.release_candidate "4f1a9c30-7b52-4e18-9d66-2c8a3f5e1b04/IOS/1.4.0/42"

# A bare build ID is not accepted: it cannot be turned back into the build
# number and train without further requests.
```
